source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I think we're getting closer. I'd like to continue exploring the V before moving back to the full wordmark.

The concepts are moving in the right direction, but they still feel rooted in calligraphy. I'd like to continue moving toward a solution where the character comes from proportion and construction rather than gesture.

I'd love to continue exploring the right arm by varying:

\* Angle
\* Width
\* Length
\* Termination
\* Relationship to the left arm
\* Transition into the vertex

I'd like every decision to feel necessary rather than expressive. The beauty should come from proportion, geometry, and construction—not added details.

value_updates.construction_basis: character must come from proportion and construction rather than calligraphic gesture
value_updates.design_necessity_rule: every geometric decision should feel necessary rather than expressive

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

First of all, THANK YOU for all of the work you are putting into this. I genuinely appreciate the level of thought and exploration you've brought to the project. It's been exciting to see the process become more and more disciplined with each round.

The blueprint studies have been especially valuable because they've allowed me to evaluate the underlying construction rather than just the finished silhouette.

One thing this round clarified for me is that posture and overall proportion have a much greater impact than terminal details alone. I consistently found myself responding more to the overall balance and construction of the letter than to any individual termination treatment.

Another realization is that I think the identity of the V is more likely to emerge from a governing structural rule than from a single distinctive detail.

The direction I'd like to continue exploring is a right arm that follows its own structural logic while remaining inseparable from the V as a whole. I don't want the distinction to come from an overlap, a joint, or another isolated feature. Rather, I'd like the entire right arm to feel as though it was conceived differently from the left while still belonging to the same letter. Every distinctive feature should feel structurally necessary rather than stylistically chosen.

I also think the left arm can continue to simplify. I'd like to move further away from traditional Roman flares and toward a cleaner, more quietly resolved termination. In several of the studies, I found that reducing those classical cues allowed the right arm to carry more of the letter's identity without feeling decorative.

One interesting observation from reviewing the blueprint studies is that I often found myself more excited by the construction drawings than the finished silhouettes. That tells me we're getting very close to the underlying idea, even if the final execution isn't completely there yet.

I don't feel the need to introduce new concepts at this stage. I think the opportunity is to continue refining the structural philosophy of the hero V until it feels inevitable. My instinct is that once the hero V is fully resolved, the smaller V, the É accent, and ultimately the rest of the wordmark will naturally follow from the same geometry.

We have made some incredible progress, and I'm excited to continue refining this direction.

value_updates.design_priority: overall posture, proportion, balance, and construction over isolated terminal details
value_updates.right_arm_design_rule: a distinct governing structural logic that remains inseparable from the complete V
value_updates.left_arm_style: clean, quietly resolved termination without traditional Roman flares
